result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers correctly put body text on background at about 1.7:1, call it the top problem, and propose almost the same warm cream, charcoal and teal palette. B is more specific about why the buttons fail: the primary is only about 2.3:1 against the page, and primary and secondary look alike. It also names the dingy tan background as a source of the muddiness and keeps some of the original colors. A's luminance range is more accurate than B's loose '40–50% lightness' claim, but B's diagnosis is more useful overall. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers give the same correct text-on-background contrast (~1.7:1) and suggest nearly the same warm cream, charcoal and teal fix. B describes the value range more accurately: A puts all the colors at roughly 40–50% lightness, which doesn't fit the light background. B also checks white text on the primary button (~4:1), clearly names body text as the first fix and gives a fuller role-by-role palette. A is tighter and handles the error color sensibly, but it doesn't pick out the primary and secondary buttons' lack of distinction as sharply.
